# Veylor

> Veylor is a self-custodial, open-source wallet for shielded ZEC (Zcash) and 0zkUSDC (USDC shielded in Railgun on Ethereum), with an atomic, trustless bridge between the two built in.

## Facts

- Platforms: Android (Google Play, or a direct APK), Windows and Linux. iPhone is a TestFlight beta. Mac is coming.
- Custody: self-custodial. There is no account. One recovery phrase restores both ZEC and 0zkUSDC, and it stays in the device's secure storage.
- ZEC is held in Zcash's own shielded pool.
- 0zkUSDC is USDC shielded in Railgun, a non-custodial privacy system on Ethereum, at the wallet's own 0zk address. A USDC deposit is public on Ethereum until it shields, and so is a withdrawal. Between 0zk addresses, nothing is.
- The bridge swaps shielded ZEC and 0zkUSDC with no custodian. It locks the USDC in a public Ethereum contract first, the ZEC goes to a fresh shielded address whose key is split between the user and the bridge, and a swap that stalls ends in a refund. The ZEC never leaves the shielded pool.
- Status: the bridge is in beta on mainnet with real funds. Each swap is capped, the app uses a single bridge for now, and no audit is published.
- Also in the wallet: Keystone and Ledger hardware wallets, Tor, private queries, coinholder voting, and English, Korean and Chinese.
- Veylor is built on Vizor (https://vizor.cash/) and published by Zapp LLC. Contact: hello@veylor.cash.

## Pages

- [Veylor](https://veylor.cash/): the wallet, 0zkUSDC, the bridge in brief, the FAQ and where to get the app.
- [How the bridge works](https://veylor.cash/how-it-works/): a swap step by step, what happens if something goes wrong, and how it compares with NEAR Intents.
- [Releases](https://veylor.cash/releases/): every download with its SHA-256 and GitHub's signed record of its build, and how to verify one.
- [Privacy policy](https://veylor.cash/privacy/): what the app keeps on the device and every network service it contacts.
- [Support Veylor](https://veylor.cash/support-veylor/): the ZEC donation address.
